subject: SIG: Deployment-mode annotations and follow-up items for Acme (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Alex Conway <alex.conway@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: Need clarity on hosting modes + artifacts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our SIG intake yesterday. We’re working through the hosting section and have a couple of follow-ups specific to deployment boundaries: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem). Our security and procurement teams need concise explanations we can attach to the SIG matrix, plus any evidence artifacts that map to each mode (network diagrams, encryption/KMS notes, ownership of logs, SLA language).

Could you:
- Provide a short side-by-side explanation we can paste into the SIG comments column (1–3 bullets per mode).
- Share any supporting artifacts (network diagram, reference matrix) that show responsibilities and evidence paths.
- Flag any items that require procurement lead time (e.g., on-prem packaging, contract amendments).

Also please cc procurement@acme-corp.com on anything that will land in the RFP/contract packet. We’d like a draft by early next week if possible — our renewal committee reviews SIGs on Monday.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Senior Cloud Security Manager
Acme Corporation
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Conway <alex.conway@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Need clarity on hosting modes + artifacts

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask. I’ve sketched a short, SIG-friendly annotation below and attached two artifacts: a filled response matrix (SIG_response_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a simplified network topology (network_topology_drawio.png). Quick notes first:

Hosted (Redwood API - shared tenancy):
- Responsibility: Redwood manages runtime, model hosting, and control plane; customer controls prompt data and API keys.
- Data residency: region-specific endpoints; we can route requests to region to meet data residency constraints.
- Evidence: SOC 2, per-route audit logs, hosted-region diagram (see attachment).

Dedicated (reserved capacity - single-tenant pool):
- Responsibility: Redwood provides dedicated GPU pool and control plane; tenant isolation at runtime with configurable VPC peering or private endpoint.
- Data residency & isolation: stronger isolation guarantees; lower noisy-neighbour risk.
- Evidence: capacity reservation docs, SLA excerpt, network peering diagram.

Private (VPC / On-prem package):
- Responsibility: Customer-managed compute/network; Redwood provides control-plane integrations or a private control plane option.
- Data flow: customer-owned network and keys (optional KMS/HSM integration); on-prem requires provisioning window and separate install artifacts.
- Evidence: deployment runbook, KMS integration guide, on-prem install checklist.

Procurement lead time & notes:
- Private/on-prem installs typically require 4–8 weeks for environment prep and validation.
- Dedicated commitments require contract-side reservation and minimum term (we flagged this in the attached matrix).
- Hosted is fastest to onboard (days) and is often chosen for POC/early prod.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll drop the attached matrix into your SIG spreadsheet and highlight the rows you asked for.
2) Marissa will provide two short evidence statements (KMS, audit logs) that you can paste into the SIG.
3) Ben will coordinate a 30-min walkthrough for procurement + security to review evidence and timelines.

Attachments: SIG_response_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), network_topology_drawio.png (image)

If that timeline works I’ll follow up with proposed slots for the walkthrough.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Conway <alex.conway@acme-corp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Need clarity on hosting modes + artifacts

Hi Alex — adding a couple of evidence-ready statements you can paste into the SIG comments column:

KMS & key ownership:
- Hosted: Customer keys may be stored in Redwood-managed KMS; we offer BYOK via integrations with customer-managed KMS providers. Access to keys used for encryption at rest is restricted to a small, audited operator group; key-rotation and audit events are logged and available via the audit trail.
- Dedicated / Private: BYOK is the recommended pattern; for Private/on-prem, keys remain in customer-controlled HSMs per contract.

Network & egress controls:
- Hosted: TLS in transit, region-scoped endpoints, and per-route allowlisting. We log all egress events and provide time-series export for audits.
- Dedicated: Support for VPC peering and private endpoints to eliminate internet egress.
- Private: Runs inside customer network; Redwood’s on-prem package contains a validated egress policy template you can adapt.

Audit logs & retention:
- Hosted/Dedicated: Per-account audit logs retained per SOC 2 policy (configurable retention windows for enterprise customers).
- Private: Retention controlled by customer.

Note on evidence artifacts: the attached matrix maps each SIG question to a primary artifact (policy, diagram, or log excerpt). For any SOC 2 or control evidence you need redacted examples, we can produce an extract under NDA.

-Marissa
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Conway <alex.conway@acme-corp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Need clarity on hosting modes + artifacts

Alex — adding a commercial / onboarding note: Dedicated requires a minimum reservation term (we usually see 6–12 months) for the capacity discount and SLA. If Acme prefers a hybrid approach we can propose a canary/backfill fallback where Hosted handles burst and Dedicated covers steady-state (we’ve put an example in the attached matrix).

Would you like procurement on the call? I can invite our contracts lead if you want to discuss reservation language and timing.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — that reads well and should cover most of our SIG questions. Two quick asks before we route the SIG to procurement: 
1) Can you upload the filled matrix into our shared Drive (link preferred) so procurement can attach it to the RFP?
2) Proposed times for the walkthrough: Mon 20 Mar 10:00–10:30am PT or Tue 21 Mar 9:00–9:30am PT. Please let me know which works and include your contracts/procurement lead if we’ll discuss Dedicated terms.

If you prefer I’ll draft the procurement email and point them at the Drive link once you upload.

Alex
Senior Cloud Security Manager
Acme Corporation
